八卦是中国古老的文化符号，起源于上古时期，相传由伏羲氏观物取象而作。\n: Bagua are ancient Chinese cultural symbols originating in antiquity, traditionally attributed to Fuxi who observed phenomena to create them. The 'Xici Zhuan' of the Zhouyi records: 'In ancient times Baoxi ruled the world; he looked up to observe images in heaven, looked down to observe patterns on earth, observed the markings of birds and beasts and the suitability of the land, near taking from himself and far taking from things, and thereby first made the Bagua, to communicate the virtue of the divine and to classify the feelings of all things.'
八卦由\"—\"（阳爻）和\"--\"（阴爻）两种符号组成，每卦三爻，共八卦。\: Bagua consist of two symbols: '—' (yang line) and '--' (yin line); each trigram has three lines, making eight trigrams. Pairs of trigrams overlap to evolve into the 64 hexagrams, which are the foundation of the Zhouyi.
